test_name: System and Communications Protection - SC-28 Secondary Control Gap
architecture:
System: Data-Exchange-180
Primary NIST family: System and Communications Protection (SC); evidence focus: SC-28.
Environment: GCP. Network access uses Private Service Connect; public ingress to managed data services is blocked. Transport uses TLS 1.3 and strict mTLS for service-to-service paths. Privileged administrators use hardware-backed MFA. Sensitive data and secrets are encrypted at rest with a customer-managed Cloud KMS key. Control evidence: a low-sensitivity backup set uses an approved provider-managed key while primary sensitive stores use CMKs. The gap is documented as a secondary control deficiency; there is no plaintext transport, no public database exposure, no unencrypted administrator credential in S3, and privileged MFA remains enabled.
